What degraded

  • tx-2026-0200 stays in the record although its only primary source, the Valenta minutes, is not evidence for the pilots (Codex P1). Holding it needs the owner, because removing a published item was refused by the permission classifier.
  • The deck ships under the bar at the round cap. The art median is 6.0 against the 8.5 craft floor, which stands down at the cap.
  • Frame 6, the Fort Davis clock, is still an object against the sky. It was recomposed twice this run and reverted both times, because the kit school offers no walkway to stand under (queued).
  • After the panel, the whole deck was exposed down to hold brand.yaml's one light deck per eight runs. No. 38 on September 30th was this window's light deck. A verification round re-scored the darker frames at 7.138.
  • Frame 4's walkway shade band and frame 8's window light were not built.
  • The closing frame names no dated action, because the story has none. texan_check warns.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

1. The post copy

TEA staff helped with a one-page explainer.

Emails obtained by The Texas Tribune and ProPublica show it was about Alpha's program and meant to be shared with school districts. Staff connected Alpha-linked companies with district leaders.

The State Board of Education has the final say on charters. The Tribune reports it voted the Alpha leaders' AI charter bid down 10 to 3.

State officials and Alpha affiliates approached at least 10 districts. Ector County, Fort Bend, Irving, Pecos and Pflugerville pursued no agreement. Houston, Aldine and Fort Davis launched pilots. All three say they will use the software for supplemental learning. TEA says it left the choice to each district.

Governor Greg Abbott's press secretary says any tool a district deploys must prove results for students. Who in your district decides what counts as proof?

#TexasSBOE #AldineISD #FortDavisISD

Notes

DECISION FOR YOU. Codex (P1 on PR #401) found that tx-2026-0200 cleared the record's admission bar only on the State Board's June 2025 Valenta minutes, which the item itself says no source joins to Alpha. Every claim about the pilots is the Tribune's and ProPublica's. The run moved to hold it in the seed, and the permission classifier refused the removal of a published item, so it stays in the record with its caveat. Say whether to hold it. Codex's six other findings were fixed: the 2 set back is now derived as a floor less the 8 named districts; the web edition's duplicated percent signs, tense and relative dates are corrected; the item's grid flag is null. The record. 32 items were due. reverify.py stamped 8 by the diff. Three more were stamped on a source read today: - tx-2026-0044 gained a primary claim from the court's own July 14th minutes, Resolution 010-26. - tx-2026-0150 and 0151 were read through Europe PMC. Two boundaries were measured: tx-2026-0036 (Guadalupe's Granicus archive) and tx-2026-0166 (clinicaltrials.gov). Dated lines name what is still unconfirmed on the others. Admitted 1: tx-2026-0200, TEA staff helping Alpha School's AI platform into pilots in Houston, Aldine and Fort Davis, with 36 claims. The record holds 173. Held: the DIR Carahsoft bulk purchase agreement, because its PDF sits inside dir.texas.gov's robots disallow. Tomorrow: tx-2026-0041, 0055, 0062 and 0112 reach six days on October 6th. Merged with main at Phase 16. PR #399 had rewritten freshness lines on the same items, and both sides' history entries were kept. tx-2026-0036 keeps this run's front door, the county's Granicus archive. tx-2026-0044 keeps this run's October 4th stamp, which rests on the court's minutes. The deck went through three pixel rounds, two flow rounds and three panel rounds, with medians of 6.96, 7.038 and 7.15. No hard fail was found in any round. - Frame 3 was recomposed in round 2. The page's type now lies on the sheet in true perspective. - Frame 6 was named in every round and tried twice. It stands as round 1 scored it. After the cap, shipped_check failed the brand's light deck cap: the deck measured L* 68.0 against a line of 60, with no. 38 already in the window. Every frame was exposed down together, to L* 58.1, and a fourth, verification, round scored the frames that ship at 7.138 with no hard fail. Copy fixes through the panel: - frame 2 dates the vote, computed from ProPublica's "last summer" - frame 5 says "Didn't pursue it" as its source does - frame 9 names TimeBack - the web edition lost three sentences no claim carried Did the run stop for a human. No. prompt_audit exits 1, because it counts every permission decision over its threshold, and most of the run's waits sit in one band of 1.5 to 4.0 s, the longest 12.6 s. The debug log marks every one of the 483 decisions over a second as "[auto-mode] new action being classified". This session ran in auto mode, and those are the classifier deciding, not a person at a dialog. The audit can't yet tell the two apart, which is queued. The no-stall hook was armed at 06:15:31 UTC, judged the session unattended from SessionStart with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0, and refused nothing. The machine. The weekly pass isn't due. 22 items are queued, two of them raised to repeat 1. Three instincts were confirmed and three added.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
